summary: The change is failure-transparent and, if anything, removes a silent-decay mechanism rather than adding one. The product-code diff is a widened regex character class (Unicode's Quotation_Mark property), two added named marks, and export keywords; the lexer stays total — every non-opening quote-like mark outside a quotation still becomes a violation token, never prose, and no try/catch, fallback, or deleted assertion appears anywhere in the diff. The one structural limit in scope (astral ornaments 🙶🙷🙸 pass as prose because the lexer reads UTF-16 units) is stated in the code comment and README rather than hidden, and is loudly caught: I verified at runtime that Node 26's \p{Quotation_Mark} data has zero astral members (42 scanned, all BMP, matching the comment's claim), and the story's demonstrated-red sabotage Q3 shows the iteration test fails if such a mark is ever listed or a future Unicode version adds one. The test diff strengthens surfacing: the hand-typed mark copy — which would have silently stopped covering the list the day a mark was added — is replaced by iterating the exported constant plus an independently computed Unicode scan, guarded by an explicit anti-vacuity assertion (UNICODE_QUOTATION_MARKS.length > 0, with a message naming the hazard), and a new floor test covers removal of historically closed marks. (Suite not runnable in this network-restricted worktree; Unicode behavior verified directly with node against the same regexes.)
